contract.note: Assessing the named dialogue system, including external factual grounding, is a fair technical reading of the categorical claim that it does not even attempt connection. This reading does not equate retrieval with philosophical understanding or sentience.

The company disclosure confirms next-token pretraining while describing additional objectives and fine-tuning. The accurate pretraining component does not establish the restrictive claim about the complete system.

reviews.rationale: The developer paper documents an explicit attempt to ground LaMDA through external information and tools within the target period. Next-token prediction remains part of the system, but does not rescue the categorical restriction. The evidence does not establish sentience or philosophical understanding.

semantics.note: The normalization accurately isolates the firm historical contribution claim. The preceding doubt about name recognition does not qualify this separate assertion.

contract.note: Substantive downstream reuse is an ordinary lasting contribution to AI. Requiring foundational transformation would unduly narrow the categorical claim. Excluding publicity and citations alone is fair.

evidence.note: A project participant identifies reworked Eugene Goostman technology underlying Emelya, with development, release and testing dated before June 2022. The retrospective disclosure was available before evaluation; it is not independently audited.
The 2016 study establishes substantive comparative research use, but its group-level findings do not independently establish an enduring contribution attributable specifically to Eugene Goostman.

reviews.rationale: The dated participant account traces Eugene Goostman's language-analysis technology into a later robot developed and used within the target period. That substantive technical reuse contradicts a zero-contribution claim under the fair ordinary reading, despite uncertainty about the amount of original code retained.
